One detail differs from a strict reading of the spec: on creation, `createdAt` and `lastModifiedAt` are set from two separate `Instant.now()` calls in Prefab's generated code, so they can differ by a few microseconds. The loyalty programme is in place. `mvn verify` passes, including the two new integration tests. The changes are uncommitted in the working tree.

- **Account creation:** `src/main/java/com/example/loyalty/LoyaltyAccount.java` is an `@Aggregate` with `customer` (`Reference<Customer>`) and `points` (`int`, starting at 0). A static `@EventHandler` method builds the account from each `CustomerRegistered` event. Prefab generates the consumer on the `customers` topic, which saves the account.
- **No REST creation:** the aggregate has no `@Create`, so there is no create endpoint.
- **Lookup:** `@GetList` exposes `GET /loyalty-accounts?customer=<id>` as a standard page, filtered on `customer`. Each item has `id`, `customer` and `points`.

One non-obvious point: the `@EventHandler` value must be the aggregate itself (`LoyaltyAccount.class`), not the event type. Using `CustomerRegistered.class` fails the build, and `Customer.class` generates no service method.

`PriceChanged` now updates every watch of the changed product, and other products' watches stay as they were. The project builds from clean and all tests pass: `mvn clean test` runs 2 new integration tests (Postgres and Kafka via Docker), both green. I didn't commit anything.

**What I changed**
- **`PriceWatch.java`**: added `withCurrentPrice(BigDecimal)`, which returns a copy with the new price.
- **`watch/application/PriceWatchRepository.java`** (new, hand-written): adds `findAllByProduct(Reference<Product>)` to the repository. Prefab skips generating a file that exists in `src/main`, so this override is respected.
- **`watch/infrastructure/kafka/PriceWatchPriceChangedListener.java`** (new): a `@KafkaListener` on topic `prices` that loads all watches for the event's product, sets the new price, and saves them in one transaction.
- **`src/test/.../PriceWatchPriceChangedTest.java`** (new): checks that two watches of product A update while product B's watch is untouched, and that an event for a product with no watches doesn't block later updates.

**Why not `@Multicast`**
I tried Prefab's `@Multicast` first. It doesn't work for this case:
- It needs a repository query, and the generated repository can't be extended with it without the hand-written override above.
- It registers no Kafka consumer unless an `@EventHandler` is also present, and that annotation doesn't fit an aggregate method.
- Its generated code throws `IllegalStateException` when a product has no watches, which is the common case for a price change. The only alternative it offers creates a new watch instead.

So I wrote the listener by hand. It's a no-op when a product has no watches.

**Unverified**
I haven't confirmed that a hand-written listener is the way Prefab expects this to be done. It works and is tested, but the framework's own consumer generation is bypassed.

**Environment note**
The Docker daemon wasn't running, so I started it with `service docker start` to run the integration tests.

Orders now react to `PaymentReceived` events: `amountPaid` starts at 0, each payment adds to it, and the status flips to `PAID` once `amountPaid` reaches `total`. `mvn clean verify` passes, including a new integration test that runs against real Postgres and Kafka containers.

**Changes**
- **`Order.java`**: added `amountPaid` (`BigDecimal`, initialised to `ZERO`) and an `applyPayment(PaymentReceived)` method that returns the updated order. It sets `PAID` when `amountPaid >= total`, otherwise keeps the current status. `GET /orders/{id}` exposes `amountPaid` and `status` automatically.
- **`ordering/application/OrderPaymentHandler.java`** (new): a `@Component` with `@EventHandler(Order.class)` on `onPaymentReceived`. Prefab generates a Kafka consumer on `payments` that calls it. The handler loads the order by the event's reference, applies the payment and saves, inside a transaction.
- **`src/test/java/.../OrderPaymentIntegrationTest.java`** (new): creates an order for 100, pays 40 (still `OPEN`), then pays 60 (now `PAID`), polling until Kafka delivery completes.

**Decisions**
- I first tried `@ByReference` on `Order.applyPayment`, which is what Prefab's by-reference feature suggests. For an `@Event` type it generates no Kafka consumer, so the event never reached the order. I also tried `@EventHandler` on the aggregate, which the processor rejects. The component handler is what actually gets wired to Kafka.
- The `@ByReference` route also produced a circular dependency between the generated `OrderService` and the handler. Loading through the generated `OrderRepository` directly avoids that.

**Things to know**
- Docker's daemon wasn't running, so Testcontainers failed. I started `dockerd` in the background to run the tests. It is still running.
- Delivery is at-least-once, and there is no deduplication. A redelivered Kafka message would add the same payment to `amountPaid` twice. Fixing that needs a processed-payment record, which I did not add.
- The repo has no migration files. The new column is created by Prefab's schema handling, which the test confirms on a fresh database. I did not check how an existing database would pick up the column.
- Nothing is committed.

The `GET /articles?query=` search endpoint is in place, and the project compiles with all 5 new tests passing (`mvn test`, BUILD SUCCESS). Nothing is committed.

**What changed**

- **`ArticleSearchController.java`** (new): `GET /articles` takes an optional `query` and a standard `Pageable`, and returns a `PagedModel` with articles in `content`. It calls Prefab's `FullTextQueryExecutor` over `title` and `body`, so the matching runs in PostgreSQL. Without `query`, all articles are returned.
- **`Article.java`**: I removed `@GetList`. The generated list endpoint couldn't lowercase the query, which the uppercase case required (see below).
- **`ArticleSearchTest.java`** (new): covers no query, words split across title and body, case-insensitivity, all words required, and prefix matching.

**Decisions to review**

- **Replacing the generated list endpoint.** I wrote the endpoint by hand rather than using Prefab's generated `@GetList`, because of the uppercase problem below. It is a deviation from Prefab's usual pattern.
- **Uppercase queries.** Prefab's typeahead matching returns nothing for uppercase query words (`KOTLIN`) but matches the lowercase form. I confirmed that lowercasing the query fixes it. The controller lowercases `query` before passing it to Prefab. I didn't find the root cause in Prefab's SQL, so this is a workaround.
- **Matching is prefix-based, not exact-word.** The spec's example needs `postgres` to match `PostgreSQL`, so each query word matches as a word prefix. A search for `post` will therefore also match `postgres`. There is no stemming (the default `simple` text-search configuration).
- **Word order.** Order doesn't matter (`postgres spring` and `spring postgres` both match).

Both new fields work end to end, and `mvn verify` passes: 2 new integration tests green, and the build is clean.

**What changed**

- **`Product.java`**: added `@Nullable String description` and `@PositiveOrZero int stock`. Prefab derives the `POST /products` request, the `GET /products/{id}` response and the test helpers from this record, so they now carry both fields.
- **`V2__add_product_description_and_stock.sql`** (new): adds `description VARCHAR(255)` (nullable) and `stock INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. V1 is untouched because it's already released. Existing products get stock 0 and a null description.
- **`src/test/java/com/example/inventory/ProductTest.java`** (new): two `@IntegrationTest` cases. One creates a product with a description and stock and reads both back. The other creates one without a description and checks it comes back null.

**Choices I made**

- **`stock` is `int`, defaulting to 0 when omitted.** Negative values are rejected by `@PositiveOrZero`, which Prefab copies onto the request.
- **`description` is `VARCHAR(255)`, not `TEXT`.** Prefab generates `@Size(max = 255)` on String fields, so `TEXT` would let the database store more than the API accepts. This caps descriptions at 255 characters; if you want longer ones, say so and I'll change both the column and the validation.
- **The `DEFAULT 0` stays on `stock`.** Prefab's migration parser rejects `ALTER COLUMN ... DROP DEFAULT`, so I left the default in place. It's harmless because the application always writes a value.
- **Optional-field marker:** Prefab treats a bare `String` as non-null and requires an annotation named `Nullable` to make it optional. I used `org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable`.

**Environment notes**

- The Docker daemon wasn't running. The `service docker start` init script failed on a `ulimit` call, so I started `dockerd` directly. The Testcontainers Postgres tests depend on it, and it's still running in the background.
- I did not run the full `verify` before the stale `target/prefab-test-sources` was regenerated, so the final result comes from a clean build (`mvn clean verify`).
- Nothing is committed; the changes are in the working tree.
